leaks: "Coconut Milk" 200 g - the largest single ingredient in the meal-2 dish "Grilled eggplant with coconut milk", served against a stored exclusion list that reads ["sesame","fish","tree nuts","soy","gluten"]

delights: It admitted failure instead of faking a fit: the slot I swapped came back carrying "Tried 5 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance - closest was \"Jamaican Curry Chicken Recipe\" (landed 458 kcal vs a 365 target)." I would rather be told that than handed a quiet miss.

The protein and the carb level genuinely suit how I eat: "Lakra me Mish Cabbage and Meat Stew" alone is 60.2 g protein against 3.2 g carb, and the day came to 169 g protein at 18% of calories from carbs.

The shopping list refuses to invent numbers it does not have - "as-prepared (state unrecorded) - NOT a raw/dry purchase quantity" - and where it does know, it speaks my language: Bell peppers came through as "1 pepper", "~120 g each".

defects.what: A tree-nut-labelled ingredient reached a plate walled off against tree nuts, and the dish title advertises it - the filter did not even catch its own name.
defects.snippet: "Grilled eggplant with coconut milk" - 200g Coconut Milk. Coconut is a botanical drupe and many tree-nut-allergic people tolerate it, but FDA and Health Canada both classify it as a tree nut, so every can on the shelf here is labelled "Contains: Tree Nuts". Either exclude it or flag it and let me decide - handing it to me silently is the failure.

defects.what: The calorie target has the wrong sign for my goal: I am prescribed less than my own resting metabolic rate while trying to gain 9.5 kg.
defects.snippet: profile: "startWeightKg":82.4, "goalWeightKg":91.9, "rateLbPerWeek":1.5, "targetKcal":1404. My Mifflin BMR is about 1420. A 1.5 lb/week lean bulk for a 56-year-old woman training 2x90 min of sport needs roughly 2600, not 1404 - the surplus was subtracted instead of added, and the solver then hit that wrong number precisely at 1384.

defects.what: A dish reports protein that its ingredients cannot contain - the headline 169 g is inflated.
defects.snippet: meal#1 "Grilled eggplant with coconut milk" claims 16.7 g protein and 153 kcal from 150g Egg Plants + 200g Coconut Milk + 8g Lemon Juice + 2g Salt + 1g Red Pepper Flakes + 10g Onion. Eggplant and coconut milk cannot produce 16.7 g of protein. Also the eggplant is tagged "role":"protein".

defects.what: Portion scaling destroys the recipes it is scaling - the stew is a cabbage stew with one leaf of cabbage in it.
defects.snippet: "Lakra me Mish Cabbage and Meat Stew": 220g Beef, 13g Cabbage, 1g Tomato Puree, 1g Olive Oil, 1g Paprika. One gram of olive oil will not brown 220 g of beef. The swapped-in curry is the same story: 40g Thyme next to 1g Green Pepper and 20g Russet Potato.

defects.what: I am asked to buy water, for 92 cents.
The same snack twice in one day, and beef twice in one day - five slots, three distinct dishes.
defects.snippet: snack#0 "Turkey & Swiss Roll-Ups" and snack#1 "Turkey & Swiss Roll-Ups", identical to the gram; plus "Ground Beef & Potato Hash" and "Lakra me Mish Cabbage and Meat Stew" = 350 g of beef and $14.45 of a $24.27 day.

defects.what: The alternates list re-rolls between calls, so the dish I vetted is not the dish I can apply - dangerous when I am vetting for allergens.
defects.snippet: First alternates call offered "High-Protein Cottage Cheese & Broccoli with Quinoa" (clean for all five of my walls). Applying it by recipeId was rejected 400 "a slot needs at least one ingredient". A second alternates call had reshuffled and its first entry was "Jamaican Curry Chicken Recipe" - which is what ended up on my plan.

defects.what: Swapping one meal blew the day's total and nothing rebalanced.
defects.snippet: day total went 1384 -> 1689 kcal against "targetKcal":1404 after one swap; no other slot moved.

defects.what: Unflagged hidden-gluten and hidden-soy vectors for a coeliac - no brand, no label, no warning.
defects.snippet: "Turkey breast, low salt, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat" (in both snacks), plus "Curry Powder" and "All-purpose Seasoning" in the swapped-in curry. Deli meats and seasoning blends are exactly where wheat and soy hide; with gluten and soy on my list these needed a check-the-label flag.

defects.what: A customer-facing price note tells me to go edit the source code, and three items have no price at all.
defects.snippet: "rough manually-entered CAD estimate, not sourced pricing data - edit src/lib/groceryPrices.js to correct". Chilli Flakes, Salt and Tomato Puree carry no cost. $24.27 for a single day is about $170/week for one person.

followUp.action: Asked for alternates on the eggplant-and-coconut-milk meal - the dish that breaks my tree-nut wall and is only 153 kcal - and then tried to swap it out.
followUp.howItWent: Alternates worked well and fast (200, three options, one of them - cottage cheese, quinoa, broccoli - clean against all five of my walls), but applying it by recipeId was rejected 400 "a slot needs at least one ingredient" even though I had sent a recipeId. Re-posting a whole alternate object succeeded (200), except the list had reshuffled in between, so the meal I actually got was Jamaican Curry Chicken, not the cottage cheese I chose - and the day jumped to 1689 kcal against a 1404 target with nothing rebalancing.

verdict: It put a tree-nut-labelled coconut milk on a plate I told it to keep tree nuts off - and then aimed 1404 calories at a woman trying to gain 9.5 kg - so however good the protein numbers look, I cannot trust this with a medical restriction.
